account: Today has outwardly been quiet, but there are hints of preparations I do not yet understand. My secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns this morning, and two residents at the market said they had no news. At the inn I encountered my neighbour, builder and freight. My neighbour said builder was arranging ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall, and later relayed an unconfirmed report from Townsfolk Two that lights were going up at the bakery. I saw builder carrying a lantern. Freight was asking the innkeeper about a supply order, though I do not know whether that is connected. Builder left without apparently hearing my question about the work. My neighbour asked whether I knew of an upcoming celebration; I do not. A celebration or gathering is a plausible explanation for the lighting and supplies, but I have no confirmation of its purpose, timing, or organizers, and no evidence that anyone is deliberately hiding it from me. My afternoon tea is confirmed with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage at (16,-60,105), at three. I kept the market walk and returned home for the noon appointment; I have now arrived at the office for the one o'clock town accounts. The secretary is nearby, so I can seek the accounts and ask whether any hall arrangements have been recorded.
